about.heading: A writer shaped by Bengali heritage, world literature, deep cinema, and scientific discipline.
about.intro: Literature and cinema are not decorative pastimes or hobbies. They are essential dimensions of my intellectual identity—training my instincts for human psychology, narrative architecture, and subtext.
about.body: My intellectual formation began with extensive immersion in Bengali literature—over 300 books exploring the lyrical realism of Bibhutibhushan, the moral scrutiny of Tagore, and the existential sharpness of Manik Bandyopadhyay—before expanding into more than 100 English and world works. Alongside reading, watching more than 1,000 films over eight years has been an emotional and psychological education in character, silence, and social observation. When combined with scientific training, this produces prose that respects rigor without losing human warmth, and argument that understands narrative momentum.
quoteLines: Broad reading is not decoration. It sharpens taste, proportion, and moral judgment.
Cinema teaches what can be implied rather than stated; science teaches what must be proven.
Immersion in character and story is an apprenticeship in perception itself.

services.heading: Writing across formats, with the same standard of clarity and control.
services.intro: The categories below are practical rather than ornamental. They describe the kinds of briefs I can handle well and the tonal range I can sustain.

categories.title: Essays and thought pieces
categories.description: Long-form writing that balances reflection, argument, and style without losing coherence.

categories.title: Articles and research summaries
categories.description: Dense material translated into readable prose that preserves complexity instead of flattening it.

categories.title: Scripts and storytelling
categories.description: Narrative movement, clean pacing, and language shaped for voice, scene, and attention.

categories.title: Brand and strategic copy
categories.description: Brand language for people, products, or ideas that want sharpness rather than noise.

categories.title: Argument and analysis
categories.description: Writing that needs reasoning, structure, and an ability to hold multiple variables at once.

categories.title: Hybrid briefs
categories.description: The strongest work often lives between categories. I can combine literary tone, strategy, and research when the brief requires it.

works.heading: Three polished sample pieces that signal range.
works.intro: These are sample or placeholder pieces for presentation purposes, not claims of publication. They are designed to show voice, structure, and the kinds of assignments I can plausibly handle well.

items.title: The Reader as Instrument
items.summary: A reflective essay on why serious reading changes not just taste, but the structure of perception itself.
items.excerpt: A person is partly made of what he has learned to notice. Books matter because they alter the granularity of attention; they teach you where to look, what to distrust, and which forms of simplification to resist.

items.title: What Scientific Training Does to a Writer
items.summary: A clean analytical article on the advantages of scientific discipline in argument, explanation, and intellectual honesty.
items.excerpt: Science does not automatically make prose elegant, but it does make certain evasions harder. It trains the mind to respect sequence, evidence, and the difference between suggestion and demonstration.

items.title: Cities, Screens, and Solitude
items.summary: A short script concept that blends cultural observation with narrative atmosphere and spoken cadence.
items.excerpt: The city was loud in all the obvious ways, but the real noise was subtler: a thousand small performances occurring at once, each one asking to be mistaken for a life.

influences.heading: Grouped influences, not a decorative bookshelf.
influences.intro: The reading life here is organized by what it sharpened: moral seriousness, structural thinking, psychological depth, and attention to systems.
influences.statement: My shelf is useful to me because it creates pressure against lazy language. Literature teaches human complexity, philosophy teaches terms of precision, economics teaches systems, and cinema teaches what can be implied rather than explained.
